fix(docx): keep a numbering level's w:pPr children in schema order (#1907)

Editing one numbering level can rewrite its `w:pPr` into an order
`CT_PPrGeneral` forbids, and Word validates that order strictly — so a
document that was fine becomes one it will not open.

Two problems in one sort, and the second only shows once the first is fixed:

- `w:spacing` was missing from the order array. `Array.indexOf` returns -1 for
  it, so it sorted to the front and came out `<w:spacing/><w:tabs/><w:ind/>`
  where the schema wants tabs (10), spacing (24), ind (25).
- Anything else unlisted had the same fate. The `rPr` sort twelve lines below
  maps unknowns to 99 so they trail; this one did not, and the two disagreeing
  about the same file is what points at an oversight rather than an intent.

Both are corrected: `w:spacing` is named, and unlisted children sort last.

Three tests. Run against the original sort they fail with
`['w:tabs', 'w:spacing', 'w:ind']` expected and
`['w:spacing', 'w:tabs', 'w:ind']` produced — the first failure is the missing
array entry, and after adding only the fallback it moves to
`['w:tabs', 'w:ind', 'w:spacing']`, which is why both halves are needed.

`packages/docx-engine`: 1664 passing. One pre-existing failure, `caps the
modeled depth but keeps every paragraph of a 2000-level table`, which I
confirmed times out identically with this change stashed.

Co-authored-by: VincentCai <vincentcai@MacBook-Air-80.local>

feat(ai-provider): add Atlas Cloud as a model provider (#1917)

Atlas Cloud (https://api.atlascloud.ai/v1) is an OpenAI-compatible
gateway that serves open-weight models from DeepSeek, Z.ai, Moonshot,
Qwen and MiniMax behind one key. It is registered the same way Cheaper
Inference is: an AiProviderId, an AI_PROVIDERS entry, a fixedEndpoint
adapter and a brand mark.

Ten seeded models, each called through chatForProvider against the live
gateway before being listed. Model ids are lab-namespaced exactly as
GET /v1/models returns them; that endpoint is public, so the list is
re-checkable without a key.

Vision is declared at the provider level and refined per model:
modelLacksVision() gains an exact-match rule for the text-only ids Atlas
Cloud serves, including MiniMax M3, which takes images on MiniMax's own
API but is text-only here. The rule matches the full namespaced id so
the direct GLM and MiniMax providers keep their current behaviour, and
the existing DeepSeek V4 pattern already covers the two DeepSeek ids.
Data-URI image input — the transport the apps use — was verified against
each of the five multimodal ids.

Signed-off-by: binyangzhu000-sudo <binyangzhu000@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(docs): first-line indents in character units — 2 字符 that rescale with the font size (#1892) (#1898)

* feat(docs): Chinese first-line indents in character units — 2 字符 that rescale with the font size (#1892)

Word's Chinese paragraph dialog sizes the first-line indent in
CHARACTERS, not points: 'first line: 2 字符' writes w:firstLineChars=200
and recomputes the twips whenever the first run's font size changes.
GenOffice only offered the absolute 0.5" (1.27 cm) default, which is
wrong for CJK body text at any size other than the one it was picked
for — the complaint in #1892.

The engine already parses w:firstLineChars (Word-probed semantics: the
char unit is the first text run's size plus letter spacing, a character
special supersedes its twips twin) and cancels character indents that
an indent edit drops. What it could not do was express one. Now:

- generate.ts writes w:firstLineChars next to the twips twin when the
  format model carries charIndents, and mergePPrFormat only cancels the
  components an edit actually drops (editing 2 字符 to 3 字符 re-writes
  the unit instead of cancelling it, so Word keeps rescaling);
- ParaFormat gains directCharIndents — the subset of character indents
  the paragraph's OWN w:ind declares. A style-chain '2 字符' must show
  through as before, not become direct formatting on a round trip;
- the docs editor stores indentFirstLineChars (hundredths) as a
  paragraph attr, renders text-indent in em so the visible indent
  rescales live with the font size, and the save path writes the char
  unit back beside its twips twin;
- the Paragraph dialog's Special 'By' field gains a cm/字符 unit
  dropdown and seeds 2 字符 on East Asian text (the same default Word
  shows for Chinese), with the unit label localized in all 21 locales.

Ruler and Ctrl+Q keep working off the twips twin / the new attr's null.

* docs: keep the Chinese comments English, keeping what they said

The feature works in Chinese, and its comments quoted the Chinese UI — "2
字符", the string Word shows next to the Special By field. The
english-comments gate reads that as Chinese prose in a comment and fails, which
is why `test` died after 77 seconds before running anything.

None of the eight comments needed the localized spelling to make their point.
What they are describing is the number: two characters, two hundredths in
w:firstLineChars. Writing that in English keeps the explanation and drops the
dependency on a particular locale's UI string, which is also what the gate is
asking for.

Comment-only: nine lines, no behaviour touched. `apps/docs`
measurement-units (16) and `docx-engine` ppr-format-fidelity (20) both pass.

* fix(docs): stop rewriting style-inherited indents on an untouched save

Open a document whose Normal style carries `<w:ind w:firstLineChars="200"/>`
— the CJK template case — change nothing, save, and every pPr-less paragraph
came back as `<w:p><w:pPr><w:ind w:firstLine="480"/></w:pPr>…`, a direct indent
the document never had.

The signature that decides whether a block needs regenerating compared two
things that do not mean the same. The parser's `charIndents` is the *effective*
value with the style chain merged in, and the comment above it says so; the
editor's `nodeFormat` produced the *direct* value under the same field name. So
every inherited paragraph looked edited.

Both ends now say which they are. `nodeFormat` sets `charIndents` (what
generate and the cancel-attr merge read) and `directCharIndents` (what the
signature compares) from the same attribute, and `normalizedFormat` reads
`directCharIndents`, so the comparison is direct against direct. This is the
`nodeFormat` / `normalizedFormat` split the review described.

One test, in the suite that already carries the STYLES fixture: open, change
nothing, assert `changedCount` is 0 and that
`<w:p><w:r><w:t>plain body paragraph</w:t></w:r></w:p>` survives with no
`w:ind` frozen onto it. **It fails without this change** and passes with it; the
five existing cases in that file are unaffected.

Also `2 字符` → `2 chars` in a test title, so the hygiene check passes.

apps/docs: 343 files, all green.

---------

fix(slides,sheets,docs): make the advertised keyboard chords real bindings (#1908)

* fix(slides,sheets,docs): make the advertised keyboard chords real bindings

The new-slide tip named ⌘M in 21 locales, but ⌘M is the Minimize
accelerator: the mac chord moves to ⇧⌘M, Windows also takes
Ctrl+Shift+M beside Ctrl+M, and both ribbon tips render through
platformShortcuts so every platform sees a key that works.

The filter screentip names ⇧⌘L, bound nowhere: bind Excel's
Ctrl+Shift+L / ⌘⇧L beside the existing ⌘⇧F, and AutoSum leaves its
mac-only ⌘⇧T corner for Ctrl+Shift+T on Windows/Linux, where Univer's
own QuickSum already owns Alt+=.

⌘⌥0 / ⌘⌥- borders fired on Windows via the Windows key; they are
mac-only and now gated on the mac.

Docs redo advertised ⌘Y / Ctrl+Y with no owner: the renderer takes the
chord now, inputs and textareas keep their own history.

Markdown and HTML replace was already correct on ⌃H / Ctrl+H
(Word-for-Mac parity, ⌘H stays Hide) — the comments say so now.

Fixes #1896

* fix(slides,sheets,docs): drop the three chords that were already owned

Review found three premises that were wrong, each causing a double fire:

- Docs ⌘Y/Ctrl+Y: Tiptap's UndoRedo keymap already binds Mod-y, so the
  window-level handler redid twice with the editor focused. The block
  is gone; the registry's ⇧⌘Z / ⌘Y line stays true through the editor.
- Sheets Ctrl/⌘+Shift+L: Univer's SmartToggleFilterShortcut owns the
  chord and our bubble listener ignored defaultPrevented, so the new
  KeyL row toggled the filter twice (a net no-op). The row is gone and
  the tests now pin that it stays gone; the screentip stays platform-
  rendered, now made true by Univer itself.
- Slides: PowerPoint for Mac's real New Slide chord is ⇧⌘N — restored
  (the ⇧⌘M detour and the Ctrl+Shift+M alias are reverted). The screentip
  text no longer carries a chord in the 21 locales; the key renders
  through data-tip-kbd as ⇧⌘N on mac and Ctrl+M elsewhere.

fix(shell)+feat(shell): bulk-unstar actually unstars; named starred groups with list filtering (#1916)

* fix(shell): bulk removal in the Starred view now unstars instead of silently keeping the stars

Root cause: the Starred view's selection bar (and row menu) reused
removeRecent, whose main-process handler only drops the star of files
that no longer exist on disk — by design, so that cleaning the recents
list never unpins favorites. In the Starred view that meant 'remove
from list' left every still-existing file starred: the rows came
straight back on refresh and bulk unfollowing was effectively unusable.

Add a dedicated home:unstar-paths channel whose handler calls the
existing removeStarredFiles, and make the Starred view's selection bar
and row menu use it (labeled with the existing 'unstar' string in every
locale). The Recent view keeps removeRecent semantics; preload exposes
window.aiOffice.unstarPaths and HomeApi gains the matching type.

* feat(shell): named starred groups — store, home IPC, and Starred-view filtering

Starred files can now be filed into user-named groups (e.g. contracts,
project material) and the Starred view can filter on them.

Store (apps/docs/src/main/starred-files.ts, pure and unit-tested):
starred.json upgrades from a flat string[] to
{ version: 1, items: Array<{ path, group? }> }. Migration rule: a
legacy string[] read keeps every star and lands every entry in no
group; the next write persists the versioned shape. Parsing tolerates
corrupt/foreign payloads by dropping the offending entries instead of
throwing. There is no separate groups list: a group exists while at
least one entry carries its name, so creating one is assigning the
first file and a group disappears with its last member (ungroup,
unstar, or file delete — no rename/delete management, by design).

readStarredFiles/toggleStarredFile/removeStarredFiles keep their
signatures and path-keyed semantics, so every existing caller
(trackedFilesUnder, fileTargetSources, search extraPaths, recents
paging, listFolder starred flags, delete-folder/recent-removal star
clearing) works unchanged; replaceRecentFile now re-keys through the
store and keeps the entry's group. New: setStarredGroup,
readStarredGroups, readStarredGroupMap.

Shell IPC: home:starred gains an optional group query filter and
attaches group to its entries (RecentEntry.group?); new
home:starred-groups and home:set-starred-group channels with preload
and HomeApi types.

UI (Home): rows with a star get a 'move to group' item in the … menu
opening a minimal picker modal (existing groups, new-group name input,
remove-from-group). The Starred view shows group filter pills (all |
each group) under the type pills; both filters compose, sidebar counts
stay group-agnostic, and a group whose last file leaves clears the
active pill via the reload-time groups fetch. Six new strings across
all 21 locales.

feat(agent-core): the model-facing text of a document range, shared (#1882)

* feat(agent-core): the model-facing text of a document range, shared

A selection is quoted back to the model beside the blocks around it, so a
reader who marked a phone number and then selected across it got the number in
the request. Docs found that and fixed it in its own redact-view; markdown's
edit queue had the same line, reading the document a fifth time through a fifth
copy of the same functions.

The walker takes a plain node rather than a ProseMirror document, so its
properties can be pinned without a schema: a withheld span never contributes
its words, a range that clips one still gets a whole marker rather than a
fragment, and an unwithheld tree comes back out unchanged. Offsets are
ProseMirror's, so callers pass their own textBetween range straight in.

Total on purpose: anything it does not recognise passes through, because a throw
here would be a silent leak — the caller's fallback would be the unredacted text.

A subpath export rather than part of the barrel, because the barrel reaches
electron and this runs in a renderer.

tests/redact-range.test.ts is the first test this code had, and it earned its
keep: the first draft compared against a hand-rolled second walk, whose bug
looked exactly like a bug in the code under test. Replaced with properties that
need no second implementation.

Also removes scripts/fill-translate-langs.py, a one-shot migration from before
this feature whose output is not in the branch.

* fix(build): declare the workspace dep the way this repo declares them

`npm ci` died before a line of code ran — `EUNSUPPORTEDPROTOCOL`,
`Unsupported URL Type "workspace:": workspace:*`. Nothing in this
repository had ever used that protocol: every cross-package dependency
upstream is `"*"`, and npm here rejects `workspace:*`. Two files said it
anyway — packages/ui's new dependency on @genoffice/agent-core, and the
lock entry that followed it.

Now `"*"`, like @genoffice/i18n and @genoffice/pptx-render beside it.
`npm ci --dry-run` exits 0; before this it exited 1 on every branch of
the stack.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(agent-core): the range walker's boundary arithmetic, three ways

Reviewing the stack's own core before it lands:

1. A leaf before `from` contributed its leafText anyway — the leaf branch
   checked only `start < to`, so an image the selection never touched
   still put a character into the model's quote. Text and marked children
   already had both-side overlap checks; the leaf now has the same.
2. A marked node the selection never reached contributed its whole marker:
   the mark check at the top of walkInline had no bounds at all. Blocks
   carry no marks in any of the five editors' schemas, but the walker
   takes schema-less JSON on purpose, so the defensive shape deserves the
   same guard the child-level branch has.
3. Recursing into a nested inline container passed the container's open-
   token position as its content start, one early: selecting 'cd' inside
   a bold span read 'd'. `start + 1` is the first child's position.

While there, separators between blocks now count block boundaries the
range strictly crosses (the rule textBetween itself applies) instead of
counting contributions, so an empty paragraph between two selected ones
costs its line break instead of gluing the paragraphs together.

* fix(agent-core): an empty paragraph is two tokens, not one — offsets stop shifting

ProseMirror serialises a node with no content by omitting the key, but
an empty container (an empty paragraph above a selection — most Word
documents) still costs its open and close tokens. withheldNodeSize
counted it as an atom, so every offset after it read one short: the
reviewer's fuzzing had it exact without empty paragraphs (9244/9244)
and wrong in 1402/9024 cases with them.

The fix inverts the default: a non-leaf without content is an empty
container worth two, which means every app's isLeaf must now name its
atoms — docs names hardBreak, tab, math and pageBreak beside the
picture it already had. The escaped test copies (#1885/#1887) land here
too so the whole stack carries one version, and a regression test pins
the reviewer's exact repro.

* chore: retrigger CI (the push event was swallowed)

* chore: prettier the range test

* test(e2e): assert the pptx mark's unprefixed label

The e2e still expected `w:label="…"` while the writer emits

review's first blocker — `w` is WordprocessingML and is unbound inside a
DrawingML part, so `w:label` is part of what made PowerPoint offer to
repair the file. The assertion was left behind by that fix and has been
failing on this branch ever since.

Verified locally: `npx playwright test slides-redact-demo` passes, 17.1s.

feat(shell): in-app illustrated user manual — help tab, F1, search, tutorials (#1863)

* feat(shell): in-app illustrated user manual — help tab, F1, search, tutorials

Every clickable control documented, with real in-app screenshots, in one
feature (issue #1520):

Framework
- Help tab in the shell (a seventh TabKind hosting the shell renderer at
  ?mode=help), three entries: F1, the Help menu, the Home sidebar card;
  the tab cannot be closed; strings in all 21 UI languages.
- HelpScreen: grouped sidebar (Getting started / Applications / AI
  features / Files & settings), full-text search over titles and bodies
  ('/' focuses), per-page table of contents with scroll-to-heading,
  ArrowUp/ArrowDown topic walking, help:// cross-topic links.
- Markdown renderer (shared, packages/ui): heading levels now survive
  (ai-md-h1..h6 classes — chat styles unchanged), standalone image lines
  render through an opt-in images.resolve hook (chat passes none), and
  indented image lines (inside list steps) match too. The manual styles
  true typographic tiers from those classes.

Content (zh + en, 14 topics)
- Every application (Docs / Sheets / Slides / PDF / Markdown / HTML),
  quick start, Home, tabs & windows, the AI panel, AI models, fonts,
  file operations, settings & integrations.

* fix(shell): a crash on every editor switch, from a separator Electron drops

Opening a document threw "A JavaScript error occurred in the main
process — TypeError: Invalid item" and left a modal over the editor.

`withUserGuide()` puts the manual's F1 item into whatever Help menu it
finds, and it built that item by destructuring two entries out of a
two-element template:

    const [item, separator] = Menu.buildFromTemplate([userGuide, { type: 'separator' }]).items
    submenu.insert(0, item!)
    submenu.insert(1, separator!)

Electron keeps a separator only when it sits *between* two real items; at
either end of a template it is dropped. Measured on this build:
`[item, sep]` yields one item, `[sep, item]` yields one item, `[sep]`
alone yields none, and `[a, sep, b]` yields three. So that build returned
one entry, `separator` was `undefined`, the `!` silenced the type error,
and the next `Menu.insert` threw. It went to the main process, so the
whole window went with it.

The template now has a third, discarded entry so the separator lands in
the middle, and the insert is guarded on its type rather than asserted.

The regression test drives the real application menu — a unit test cannot
see this, because the defect is in how Electron assembles a template
rather than in a pure function. Reverting the fix turns it red in 3.1s
with the same `TypeError: Invalid item`; with the fix it passes in 7.2s.

* docs(help): a keyboard shortcut reference, with the mac and Windows chords side by side

Every editor has its own bindings and only a few work everywhere, so the manual
had no single place to look. This adds one: 286 rows across Word, Sheets,
Slides, PDF, Markdown and HTML, three columns each — action, macOS, Windows and
Linux.

The platform split is the reason the page exists. It is not only a rename:
Replace is Ctrl+H on both platforms because macOS owns Command-H for Hide; Go To
is Word's Option-Command-G but Ctrl+G on Windows; Slides closes a tab with
Command-W on macOS and Ctrl+Q — which quits — everywhere else; New Slide is
Shift-Command-N on macOS and Ctrl+M off it, each a no-op on the other platform.

Every row was traced to a handler rather than inferred from a registry name.
Two consequences worth noting: Sheets' Bold, Italic, Underline, F2, Cmd+F and
Cmd+R are provided by the embedded spreadsheet engine and are not in this
repository at all, so an earlier pass that searched only the repo missed them;
and the first draft put the Sheets caveat about editing-suppresses-shortcuts on
"this page", which was wrong inside the Sheets section and is now "in Sheets".

Chords are copied into every translation byte for byte and only the action
column, the headings and the prose are translated, following the convention
pdf.<lang>.md already uses for the wheel chord. Connective words inside chord
cells — `or`, `plus the keypad`, `any key`, `type N, then` — are localised, so
a reader does not meet an English word sitting in their own key column.

Translations: all 21 UI languages. `npm run check:help-langs` is green.

Two things the file documents because both fail silently:

* docs(help): space the bold runs that Chinese text butts up against

Four CJK articles fail roundtrip-serializer.test.ts with
`Invalid collection of marks for node text: bold,bold`. The English originals
of the same two articles pass, and so does every other locale.

The trigger is a bold span whose closing `**` is followed straight away by a
CJK character. `**The content tools** take` parses; `**内容类工具**把` does not.
It is not any one line — dropping any single suspect line still fails, the two
halves of `mcp.zh.md` each pass alone and fail together, and removing every
`**` from the file passes. Whatever accumulates, it only does so once a
document carries enough of these.

A space after the closing `**` fixes it and matches how the English source
writes the same sentence, so the mixed-script spacing ends up reading
correctly rather than merely parsing. Bold followed by full-width punctuation
is left alone: `**⋯ 菜单** 提供：` wants no space, and adding one there would
put it before the colon.

See #1899.

`AiProviderConfig.apiKey` lives inside `AiSettings`, and `setAiSettings`

fix(cli): stop linking into the Homebrew prefix without asking (#1918)

On macOS the app created `genoffice` a few seconds after every launch, and on a
brew machine the first writable system directory it found was
`/opt/homebrew/bin` — the Homebrew prefix on Apple Silicon, and the classic one
on Intel. `$(brew --prefix)/bin` is a directory Homebrew manages itself: the
link is untracked by brew, dangles once the app is removed, and comes back on
the next launch. Homebrew declined a cask PR over exactly this, and three
earlier ones for the same behaviour.

The user's own directory is already in the candidate list (#1019), and it is
what a non-admin install falls back to, so removing the brew prefix does not
cost anyone the command — it only stops the uninvited write. A user who wants
the link there can still ask for it by hand; what is gone is the app doing it
for them.

`defaultCandidateDirs` now offers `/usr/local/bin` (still a candidate on Intel
machines that use the classic prefix, and still the PATH every login shell
reads) and then `$XDG_BIN_HOME` / `~/.local/bin`.

Two tests. The candidate-list one **fails without this change** — `/opt/homebrew/bin`
is present in the darwin list — and the second pins that a walk given only a
locked directory and a user directory links into the user one and nowhere else.
